title: To Africanus: greeting; Susanna in Daniel
english: Origen to Africanus, beloved brother in God the Father through Jesus Christ his holy Child: greetings. Your letter raised the question of the story of [[Susanna >> Bible:Daniel 13:1-64]] carried with Daniel among us — whether it is authentic Scripture or a later addition — after I had used it in discourse with our companion Bassus.

title: Ep. Afr. 2–5: Hebrew copies vs church books; Job and other pluses
english: You objected that I used Susanna as if unaware some call it uncanonical. I answer from the wider fact: in many holy books we find more or less than the Hebrews transmit — in Job and elsewhere verses stand with us that are absent there, and the church’s edification has long received these books. Still I do not refuse to search the Jewish copies; I refuse to [[move the ancient landmarks >> Bible:Proverbs 22:28]] set for the churches.

title: Ep. Afr. 6–10: Susanna’s Greek wordplay; elders; Spirit in the story
english: The story’s Greek plays on names and trees are not a decisive strike against it; translation and retelling can carry such features. The Spirit’s work in exposing the elders and vindicating Susanna fits the God who [[rescues the innocent >> Bible:Daniel 13:60-62]] and judges false witness.

title: Ep. Afr. 11–18: Church use; closing counsel — AFRICANUS CLOSEOUT
english: I do not scorn Hebrew truth, yet I will not surrender to a few what the churches have held for building up those [[bought with a price >> Bible:1 Corinthians 6:20]]. Use both care and charity: test the copies, keep the peace of the churches, and let love for those for whom Christ died govern the dispute. AFRICANUS CLOSEOUT.

title: To Gregory: greeting; natural gifts need training
english: Greetings in God, my lord, most earnest and honored son Gregory, from Origen. Natural aptitude, as you know, can bear fruit when it takes on training and presses toward the end of whatever one means to practice. Your gifts could make you a finished Roman lawyer or a notable Greek philosopher of one of the esteemed schools — but I would have your whole ability brought as an offering to Christianity.

title: Philosophy as handmaid; plunder the Egyptians
english: Take from Greek learning what serves the interpretation of the holy Scriptures — as Israel once took Egyptian goods for the tabernacle — but do not stay in Egypt. Philosophy is a handmaid if it leads to Christ; a mistress if it [[takes you captive >> Bible:Colossians 2:8]].

added_allusions.reason: Distinctive image, not generic theme: Israel taking Egyptian goods for the tabernacle, applied to Greek learning serving Scripture.

title: Ask, seek, knock — GREGORY CLOSEOUT SERIES CLOSEOUT
english: Above all, attend to the reading of the divine Scriptures with prayer. [[Ask, and it will be given; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened >> Bible:Matthew 7:7]]. Bring your trained mind as an offering, and let the Word be the end of the journey.
